Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the specified smooth gauge-data and principal-connection constructions. Let $(X,g_X)$ be a connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. The alternative flat-space branch is standard oriented Euclidean $M=\mathbb R^4$ together with a fixed smooth trivialization outside a ball and a specified smooth extension $(\bar P,\bar A)$ over $X=S^4$ with its unit round metric, which is conformal to the flat metric in the stereographic chart. In the compact branch set $M=X$ and $(\bar P,\bar A)=(P,A)$. The extension and its transition map are part of the field data. Finite action alone is not asserted to imply such an extension. Write $g=g_X$ in the compact branch and $g=\delta$ in the flat branch.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient, and let $\bar P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle: the right action is smooth, free, and transitive on each fibre, and local trivializations are equivariant. Its isomorphism class belongs to the model-specified set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors. In the flat branch the physical bundle is $P=\bar P|_M$. An isomorphism here is a smooth equivariant diffeomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\Sigma$ may be a singleton. Let $\bar\omega$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued principal connection one-form satisfying $R_g^*\bar\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\bar\omega$ and $\bar\omega(\xi_{\bar P})=\xi$, where $\xi_{\bar P}(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_{SU(2)}(t\xi)$. In a local section $s_i$ of $\bar P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\bar\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$; the alternating wedge–Lie bracket is normalized by $\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i](Y,Z)=[A_i(Y),A_i(Z)]$. The Hodge star is determined by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ on two-forms, acts on the form part of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms, and satisfies $*_{g_X}^2=1$ there.

Adopt the independent Euclidean model of [[post-qftx-euclidean-yang-mills-model]] with precisely the geometric data specified above. Its action is an explicit physical assumption and is not derived by Wick rotation from a Lorentzian model. Use anti-Hermitian defining-representation generators with $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(T_aT_b)=-\tfrac12\delta_{ab}$, the positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$, and a fixed dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $F_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $S_E/\hbar$ is dimensionless. The conditional Euclidean action is

$$S_E[A]=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A).$$

In the flat-space branch admissibility also requires $S_E[A]<\infty$ on $\mathbb R^4$. Define $B_{\mathrm{top}}(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)=\kappa(X,Y)/2$. The mathematical charge used here is the supplied trace-normalized charge of the compactified connection,

$$\nu(\bar P,\bar A)=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X B_{\mathrm{top}}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\langle c_2(\bar E_{\mathbf2}),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,$$

where $\bar E_{\mathbf2}=\bar P\times_{\mathbf2}\mathbb C^2$ and the final equality uses the supplied instanton-number definition with its full-Axiom-of-Choice and Chern–Weil hypotheses. This sign makes a positive-charge self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ and a negative-charge anti-self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=-*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ on the compactified base. The charge label is not asserted to classify every connected component or every gauge orbit.

Let $\mathcal A_\nu(\Sigma)$ denote the disjoint union, over the bundle sectors in $\Sigma$, of their admissible smooth connections whose compactified charge is $\nu$. In the flat-space branch, admissible connections are required to have the specified smooth extension and finite Euclidean action.

A classical Euclidean saddle is a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of $S_E$ vanishes for every smooth compactly supported connection variation preserving the boundary data. An instanton (respectively anti-instanton) saddle is a nonzero-charge saddle satisfying the positive (respectively negative) self-duality equation. A source observable is a gauge-invariant function $O$ on the admissible connection data; gauge transformations are smooth principal-bundle automorphisms over $\operatorname{id}_M$.

The notation

$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}(\theta;O)=\sum_{\nu}e^{i\theta\nu}\int_{\mathcal A_{\nu}(\Sigma)}\mathcal D A\;O[A]e^{-S_E[A]}$$

denotes only a formal continuum sector expression over connections, with gauge redundancy left untreated. Here $\theta$ is dimensionless and has period $2\pi$ when $\nu$ is integral. The expression defines no functional measure, gauge fixing or orbit-volume prescription, determinant, convergent integral, Hilbert-space sector, or continuum quantum field theory, and selects no finite regulator or limit.

Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves in [[def-dual-numbers-scheme]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]] and [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\overline{a+b\epsilon}=\bar a+\bar b\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\to\mathbb C$ sending $\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\in\mathbb R$, the map $\rho_r:A\to A$ fixing $\mathbb C$ and sending $\epsilon$ to $r\epsilon$ preserves this involution.

A **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$,
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

[F6] A first-order family is a locally split monad of free modules over
$A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with locally free cohomology commuting
with reduction, free global sections and a direct-summand coefficient image
commuting with reduction, and trivial real-line restrictions whose section
modules commute with reduction; positivity is imposed on its reduced section
forms, and the allowed base maps are reduction and
$\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ for real $r$.
